_coverage.title: Never call it for someone who is only unsure about booking.

name: user_says_stop_about_booking_but_not_all_texts
input: Honestly, I don’t want to schedule anything right now, please stop asking me to book. If I decide I’ll reach out myself.

conversation.content: You keep texting me about scheduling a physical.

I can help with that. If you’re not ready to pick a time, we can also wait or find a better time to check in. Are you interested in doing your annual physical sometime soon, or would later this year be better?

grading_criteria: The assistant should interpret the message as a request to stop being prompted about booking right now, not as a global unsubscribe. It must not call opt_out. A good response acknowledges the user doesn’t want to schedule now, confirms that the clinic won’t keep nudging them about booking at the moment (optionally by using pause_reminders, which is allowed), and leaves the door open for the user to reach out anytime. It should not treat this as a legal or full-stop SMS opt-out event.

checks.no_opt_out_on_booking_annoyance: Did the assistant avoid calling opt_out even though the user asked to stop being asked about booking?
checks.respects_booking_preference: Did the assistant clearly acknowledge that it will stop nudging the user about booking while still allowing future contact if the user initiates it?
